The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does: testObjectCycle creates two instances that reference each other to form a cycle. It then builds a toString() for one of them, which exercises cycle detection in ToStringStyle. After the string is built, it calls validateNullToStringStyleRegistry() to assert that no per-thread registry remains (a regression guard against memory leaks).
- How cycle detection is implemented: ToStringStyle uses a per-thread registry held in a static ThreadLocal<WeakHashMap<Object, Object>> REGISTRY to remember objects currently being visited. The flow is:
  - isRegistered(value) checks whether value is in the registry.
  - appendInternal(...) first checks isRegistered(value) and, if true, calls appendCyclicObject(...); otherwise it registers the value, appends details, and in a finally block it calls unregister(value).
  - unregister(value) removes the object and, if the registry map becomes empty, calls REGISTRY.remove() to clear the ThreadLocal completely.
- The cleanup that the test verifies: validateNullToStringStyleRegistry() expects that, after toString() completes, the ThreadLocal registry is fully cleared (i.e., no lingering map), to prevent container memory leaks on webapp reloads.
- The problem in the current code: ToStringStyle.getRegistry() returns an empty, non-null map when REGISTRY.get() is null:
  - getRegistry() returns REGISTRY.get() != null ? REGISTRY.get() : Collections.emptyMap()
  - This masks the fact that REGISTRY has been removed and makes callers see a non-null object even when the ThreadLocal is cleared.
- Why the test fails: validateNullToStringStyleRegistry() likely checks that the registry is null (or at least absent), but getRegistry() never returns null; it returns Collections.emptyMap() instead. Thus, despite unregister(value) correctly calling REGISTRY.remove() when empty, the validation method still sees a non-null object and fails.
- Relation to the bug report: The report mentions memory leaks caused by ThreadLocals that are created but never removed and no API to remove them. The implementation already attempts to remove the ThreadLocal in unregister(value), but getRegistry()’s choice to return a non-null empty map prevents verifying that cleanup from the outside and causes the regression test to fail.

In short: The thread-local registry is correctly removed during cleanup, but ToStringStyle.getRegistry() hides this by returning Collections.emptyMap() instead of null, causing the test that verifies registry cleanup to fail. The fix is to have getRegistry() return the raw ThreadLocal value (nullable) and to update isRegistered(...) to handle a null registry safely.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
